metadata.title: The GD-1 Stellar Stream Kinematic Tail: Threshold Fragility, Spectroscopic Binarity, and Kinematics across the Spur in DESI DR2
metadata.description:
This repository contains the complete empirical data, reproduction code, verification test suites, publication figures, interactive phase-space visualizer, and manuscript for the kinematic audit of the GD-1 stellar stream in DESI DR2 (Research v43 → v47).

Key Scientific Results:

  • Threshold Fragility (v43): Demonstrates that conventional hard probability thresholding (P_thin ≥ 0.90) in the DESI DR2 catalog is statistically fragile: a single borderline star (Star 28) shifting by ΔP = −0.0166 flips global significance across α = 0.05 (p = 0.0043 → 0.0539).
  • Continuous Bayesian Scoring (v44): Continuous scoring (T_cont = 27.82, p = 0.0012) confirms the continuous tail statistic remains detectable without step-function artifacts; an audit of Star 28's 14 immediate neighbors (±3°) reveals they are dynamically cold (−1.40 km/s, −0.25σ), showing no evidence for a localized single-subhalo collision dipole.
  • Velocity Anisotropy Audit (v45): Combining DESI radial velocities with Gaia DR3 proper motions reveals extreme velocity anisotropy (R_aniso = 0.1613, 6.2× radial dominance), contradicting 3D isotropic heating. Exactly 9 stars (78.5% of tail energy) possess cold 2D proper motions (z_tan ≤ 1.36σ) and nominal single-star Gaia astrometry (RUWE ≈ 1.01). Subtracting them collapses the residual tail score to null expectation (p_residual = 0.7727).
  • Multi-Epoch Spectroscopic Variability (v46): Archival SDSS DR17 spectra show multi-epoch velocity variability across surveys. Calibrated against empirical cross-survey dispersion (σ_emp ≈ 6.98 km/s), thin stream member Gaia DR3 804386042407893376 in the spur bin exhibited a ΔV = +28.64 ± 7.17 km/s shift (≈ 3.5σ_emp, an independent recovery of the ~30 km/s variable noted in Section II of Nibauer et al. 2026), while Outlier 13 in the diffuse cocoon envelope showed ΔV = +20.60 ± 5.88 km/s (≈ 2.4σ_emp), Star 4 showed a modest drift (≈ 1.4σ_emp, consistent with noise), and Star 28 is dynamically constant (0.24σ).
  • Spatial Kinematics and Confrontation with Nibauer et al. (v47): Subtracting candidate binaries yields an intrinsic core dispersion of σ_int = 1.88 (+0.19 / -0.18) km/s (95% upper limit 2.27 km/s, a 17.1% like-for-like reduction). Direct bin-by-bin confrontation with Nibauer et al. (2026) reveals that DESI DR2 is consistent with peak dispersion in the gap/spur bin ([-40, -20]°, 3.32 to 2.72 km/s), though the elevation over the trailing (1.87 km/s) and leading (1.57 km/s) arms is modest (~1.5–2σ). This localized spur excess could stem from compact subhalo perturbations, diffuse cocoon contamination, or undetected binaries, deferring definitive forward modeling to future work.
